headline: On last trading day, Nifty gained 75 points while Sensex slipped into red; smallcaps outperformed amid dividend stock focus.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 21 September.

why: Sensex slipped into the red following profit booking in major banking and financial heavyweights.
Nifty 50 managed to gain 75 points, supported by gains in specific sectoral indices.
The market faced headwinds from rising global crude oil prices and geopolitical uncertainty.
Mixed performance was seen as investors weighed domestic policy changes against global cues.
whatHappening: Smallcap stocks witnessed buying interest, helping the Nifty index stay in positive territory.
Market participants reacted to the news of missile attacks on Saudi Aramco facilities.
Several stocks entered focus as investors prepared for upcoming dividend payouts.
Concerns over FII outflows and rising crude oil prices influenced the trading session's volatility.
summary: The Indian market ended the last session mixed with Nifty gaining 75 points while Sensex slipped into the red. Investors are currently monitoring dividend stocks and the potential impact of new EPFO wage ceiling regulations. Markets remain closed for the weekend and will reopen on Monday with a focus on geopolitical developments.
